land.text: Dar al-Kuti under Sanussi: 'centre and northwest of present-day Central African Republic', later 'much of modern CAR' (the page gives no outline; four CAR prefectures stand for it)

successors.note: The French signed a protectorate with Sanussi on 28 August 1897; after his death on 12 January 1911 France took most of the territory under direct control; Ouanda Djallé fell to Captain Souclier on 17 December 1912.

capitals.name: Chá
capitals.note: "Chá, on the Diangara River (a tributary of the Aouk), became the capital"; Rabih's lieutenants seized it in 1874 and Wadai's aguid Cherfeddine destroyed it in October 1894. The page gives no coordinates and Chá is not in the gazetteer; the point is a proxy, the gazetteer's N'Délé (same prefecture, Bamingui-Bangoran).

capitals.name: N'Délé
capitals.note: Sanussi "later founded a new fortified settlement (tata) at N'Délé" after Cha was destroyed in October 1894; the coordinates are the gazetteer's.

rulers.name: Djougoultoum
rulers.title: governor
rulers.note: First governor under Wadai; the page says the dates are "probably not exact".

rulers.name: Muhammad al-Sanussi
rulers.title: sheikh, sultan
rulers.note: Installed by Rabih in 1890; died 12 January 1911; Kamun succeeded him.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Dar al-Kuti row). In 1830 Djougoultoum settled in Bilad al-Kuti, a slave-raiding zone south of the Aouk, and became its first governor under Wadai; the state had "fourteen villages (probably only the main settlements), traversable in two days east to west". The page gives no outline.

ledger.note: 1830: Dar al-Kuti begins. "In 1830, Djougoultoum settled in Bilad al-Kuti, a slave-raiding zone south of the Aouk River, and became its first governor under Wadai" (the page says the infobox span is 1830-1911 and the text "from around 1830").

region.text: Dar al-Kuti under Sanussi: 'centre and northwest of present-day Central African Republic', later 'much of modern CAR' (the page gives no outline; four CAR prefectures stand for it)

ledger.note: About 1890: Sanussi's domain grows. "Rabih deposed Kobur and installed Kobur's nephew Muhammad al-Sanussi as sheikh of Dar al-Kuti and Dar Runga"; "under Sanussi, it expanded to include much of modern CAR" over the Banda, Nduka and other peoples. The page dates the expansion not at all; 1890 is a bridging year and the prefectures a guess.

ledger.note: 17 December 1912: Ouanda Djallé falls. After Sanussi's death (12 January 1911) France decided "to take most of the territory under direct control"; "17 December 1912: Ouanda Djallé fell to Captain Souclier. Kamun went into exile in Sudan."

wars.outcome: 28 August 1897: Sanussi and Émile Gentil signed a treaty of trade and alliance (revised 18 February 1903 and 26 January 1908) establishing a French protectorate; after his death on 12 January 1911 France took most of the territory directly; Ouanda Djallé fell on 17 December 1912.
wars.note: In 1891 Sanussi had killed Paul Crampel and his companions.

certainty.note: No outline; 'much of modern CAR' is undated and the prefectures are a guess.

notes:
Dar al-Kuti, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Dar al-Kuti (one page).

End: infobox 1911, body "until 17 December 1912" (followed). The wadai-empire ledger should carry Dar al-Kuti as a tributary until 1890 (via Dar Runga) and the state-of-rabih-az-zubayr ledger Sanussi as Rabih's sheikh from 1890 (vassal_start 1890; the end is not on this page); the french-africa ledger the protectorate of 28 August 1897 (vassal_start; revisions of 18 February 1903 and 26 January 1908). The Wadai-Dar al-Kuti ties (Dar Runga) are Wadai's. The CAR prefectures are guesses: the page says "centre and northwest" and the Aouk, Diangara and Azoum rivers; the Dar Runga domain between the Azoum and Aouk is drawn only through the 1890 prefecture union.
